subject: Reserved lanes pricing & token economics — next steps
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Li <sam.li@horizontech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-11T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Reserved lanes pricing & token economics — next steps

Sam — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on sizing and economics before the draft MA: 

Summary of HorizonTech needs (as we heard it)
- Production inference for contextual search + realtime assistant across mobile and web
- Target p95 latency ~250ms for 2k concurrent active users
- Average request length ~450 tokens; peak flows up to 2k tokens for long-form generation
- Goal monthly consumption estimate: 80M–150M tokens/month in Q1 production (scaling thereafter)

Pricing and econ questions we agreed to clarify
1) Desired target $/1M tokens goal for procurement planning (you mentioned a range at the call)
2) Preferred GPU family for reserved lanes (we outlined H100 vs A100-80GB options)
3) Throughput SLOs (tokens/sec and concurrency) to pick correct reserved banding

Immediate ask from Redwood
- Can you confirm the target $/1M tokens range (ballpark is fine) so we can tune the reserve sizing?
- Which GPU family is procurement leaning toward (H100 for max perf vs A100-80GB for cost efficiency)?
- Any constraints on contract length or commit cadence (quarterly vs annual)?

Attached: capacity_sizing_proposal_20270111.xlsx (draft bands and estimated $/1M token math) and a redlined MA template for your legal (horizon_ma_draft_20270111.pdf).

Proposed next steps
- Sam/Ava: Reply with ballpark $/1M target and GPU preference by Wed 1/13
- Redwood: We'll return a tailored reserved lanes quote + throughput validation plan by Fri 1/15
- Schedule a 30m follow-up next week to walk the SLA and canary rollout plan

Thanks — Priya

--

Subject: Re: Reserved lanes pricing & token economics — next steps

Thanks, Priya — good recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Token volume: For procurement we should model a conservative baseline of ~90M tokens/mo with a 6–9 month ramp to ~200M tokens/mo if pilot goes well. So please give both a baseline band and a scale-up band.
- Budget range: Our finance sponsor is thinking in the $120–$220 per 1M tokens range (depending on committed levels and SLA). Lower end assumes stronger reservation and multi-year commit.
- GPU preference: We're leaning toward A100-80GB due to predictability and lower up-front cost; however, if H100 is meaningfully better for your latency SLOs at similar $/1M we can consider that.

Question: For throughput planning — can you show tokens/sec per reserved lane for both GPU families, and what concurrency those lines assume? That will help us size the initial reserved lanes (we currently think 3 lanes to start).

I can confirm contract length preference: 12–24 months depending on price.

Sam
Head of ML Platforms
HorizonTech
sam.li@horizontech.com | +1 (650) 777-9988

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Li <sam.li@horizontech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-11T13:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Reserved lanes pricing & token economics — next steps

Sam — perfect, thanks for the ranges. Attached spreadsheet has the two-band quote (baseline vs scale) and an explanatory tab for unit-econ assumptions. High level for the teams: 

Reserved lanes sizing (initial proposal)
- Option A (Cost-efficient): 3 x A100-80GB lanes (reserved) — each lane estimated steady-state throughput ~9k tokens/sec for generation-heavy workloads, ~13k tokens/sec for pure embedding/reranking patterns; supports ~600 concurrent short-chat QPS with KV caching. Estimated baseline $/1M tokens: $145 (with 12-month commit) and $125 with 24-month commit at 90M/mo band.
- Option B (Performance-first): 2 x H100 lanes + 1 x A100-80GB as overflow — H100 lanes estimated ~15k tokens/sec steady-state for gen; latency gains at long sequences. Estimated baseline $/1M tokens: $185 with 12-month commit.

Notes on assumptions
- Avg token cost calc assumes 15% batching efficiency, 20% cache hit on prefix KV, and standard quantization profile (INT8 recommended for A100).
- We include automated prefix caching and adaptive batching in the reserved lanes — those are the levers that change unit economics in real traffic.

Follow-up ask
- Can your finance sponsor confirm whether $120–$220/1M is a hard band or if we should take a target of <$160 to win the pilot? We can structure a pilot-friendly 3-month introductory rate that graduates to the baseline commit.
- Confirm whether 3 lanes is acceptable as a starting reserve — we'll run a throughput validation test during canary.

I'll loop in our infra lead (Ben) to propose exact lane sizes in the attached workbook and to outline the canary validation script.

Thanks — Priya

--
Priya Natarajan

Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-01-11T16:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Reserved lanes pricing & token economics — next steps

Sam, hi — Ben from Infra here. A couple concrete numbers to help sizing and a short checklist for the validation run: 

Throughput per lane (empirical estimates based on our benchmarks)
- A100-80GB lane: ~9k tokens/sec sustained for mixed-gen workloads at 512 token avg; burst to ~12–13k tokens/sec for short-form requests 
- H100 lane: ~14–16k tokens/sec sustained for long-sequence gen (1.5k–2k tokens); better headroom for KV-heavy flows

Concurrency guide (typical map)
- 1 A100 lane ~= 500–700 concurrent short chat sessions (with KV caching and a 200ms inter-token pacing assumption)
- 1 H100 lane ~= 800–1,000 concurrent short chat sessions for the same assumptions

Validation checklist
- Provide a canonical prompt set (we need 200 sample dialogs covering your 450 token avg + 10% long sequences)
- Agree on target p95 latency cutoff for the canary (you proposed 250ms)
- Schedule a 2-hour run to collect per-token timing and cache-hit telemetry (we'll share a template test harness)

I'll update the attached workbook with lane-level TTFB and per-token cost rows. If Horizon is comfortable with A100 for the pilot, we can present a baseline $/1M of $145 (12mo) and a pilot intro of $105 for 3 months to accelerate the PO. If you want H100-first, we should plan for $175–$195/1M baseline.

Available to do the validation next Tue/Wed 1/19–1/20 — Priya, Sam, can you confirm which day works?

Cheers — Ben

--
Ben Carter
